stem: Detergents used for cleaning clothes are :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Detergents are surfactants (wetting-agent) compounds that show cleaning properties in dilute solution. In fact, such substances are alkyl benzene sulfonates. Detergents are soluble even in hard water.

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Emulsification is the process of mixing two or more immiscible liquids to form a semi-stable mixture. Soap molecules are generally long-chain compounds with polar groups; for example, soap (fatty salts of sodium and potassium). A soap molecule has two parts- (i) a long hydrocarbon chain (C H ) which is soluble in fat, and (ii) a water-soluble polar part (–COO– Na+ group). During emulsification, the non-polar alkyl part (C H ) dissolves oil or grease, while the polar part (–COO– Na+) dissolves in water. When rubbed properly, grease becomes suspended in water as tiny droplets and is easily washed away with running water.
Substances used for cleaning are called soaps and detergents. In fact, the soap that we have been using for years also falls under the detergent category.

stem: Which one of the following is used in the manufacture of soaps?
expl: When an oil or fat is mixed with sodium hydroxide solution, the oil/fat gets converted into the corresponding sodium salts of fatty acids and glycerol. This reaction is called saponification.

stem: Permanent hardness of water is due to –

options.label: a
options.text: Chlorides and sulphates of Calcium and Magnesium

expl: Hard water is water that does not produce lather easily when detergent (soap) is used. The main cause of this is the presence of chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

stem: The elements present in urea are :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Urea is an organic compound with the chemical formula NHCONH. It contains about 46.67% nitrogen, present in 2 2 the form of an amide. In organic chemistry, it is also called carbamide.

stem: Which component of fertilizer is used to encourage rapid development?
expl: Phosphorus helps in transferring energy from sunlight to plants, stimulates early root and plant growth, and speeds up maturity. Hence, option (d) is correct. Apart from phosphorus, nitrogen, potassium, etc., also help in plant growth.

stem: Which compound is known as a night-glowing pigment from below?
expl: Night-glowing pigments are substances that first absorb light energy and then keep emitting light slowly for a long time in darkness. Among the given options, europium-doped strontium aluminate is well-known and widely used as a night-glowing pigment.

stem: Which material is used for smart film?
expl: Smart film or switchable smart film is generally a PDLC (Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal) film. For the transparent conductive layer of smart film, indium tin oxide (ITO)-coated PET or glass is commonly used. Calcium carbonate (CaCO) is mainly used in cement, lime making, and as a filler; zinc chloride (ZnCl) is used in chemical reactions, dry cells, flux, etc.; and silica (SiO ) is used as a structural material for ordinary glass, etc.

stem: Which of the following is not a radioactive element?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Cadmium is classified as a transition metal, and cadmium is a chemical element; however, it is not a radioactive element. Cadmium (Cd) is a silver-colored metal with a bluish tinge. Cadmium is a toxic metal. Its most common use is in the manufacture of nickel–cadmium batteries.

stem: Which of the following is the best fire extinguisher?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the given options, carbon dioxide (CO) is a good fire extinguisher. Carbon dioxide is commonly used in fire extinguishers.

stem: The breath test conducted by police to check a drunken driver has which one of the following on the filter paper?

options.label: c
options.text: Silica gel coated with silver nitrate

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: To test the breath of a person suspected of drunk driving, the police use an instrument called a breathalyzer (breathalyser). In this device, the filter paper/chemical cartridge contains potassium dichromate (KCrO) and sulfuric acid (HSO). The orange-red potassium dichromate reagent reacts with alcohol and turns green. The intensity of the green color is used to estimate the amount of alcohol in the exhaled breath.

stem: The alphabet X in X-ray stands for _______ ray.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In X-rays, the letter X means an unknown ray. X-rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation.
